answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one real vineyard row: a river basin authority issues a single seasonal irrigation allotment per vintner, so identities cannot be flooded into existence. An inspector walks the vines in person and stamps a velvet-seal certificate, one row per day, no bulk approvals. Fruit must be sold to real buyers with proceeds logged. The registry fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real row, another season of vineyard labor, another allotment, and twice the prior fee.
